hypotheses.status: FROZEN PRIMARY — evaluated; negative verdict; terminal final-dot uniqueness stop; no TIF emitted
hypotheses.title: Signed one-sided flank-offset persistence of inverted basement steps
hypotheses.physical_signature: Signed basement-depth contrast at 2 km and 4 km across each HGM crest; same polarity and >=0.60 magnitude persistence; emit a 3-pixel ribbon.
hypotheses.why_missing_from_catalogue: A buried basin-interior fault can offset basement without preserving an exposed scarp; persistent one-sided displacement is the target.
hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Finite-width intrabasement mafic/granitic body or intrusive contact; paired edges can imitate a local step.
hypotheses.differs_from_existing: Not another HGM/throw threshold and not sibling R2's band-13/band-15 normal anti-alignment. Use sign-consistent 2 km/4 km cross-step flank persistence from the band-13-only inverted depth surface.
hypotheses.data_obtainability: The NOAA directory/readme and a partial br_depth.xyz response were verified in the browser. The complete grid is not present locally; the sandbox cannot fetch NOAA hosts from the execution environment. No GP-1012 statistics have been calculated.

hypotheses.status: PROSPECTIVE, UNTESTED ALTERNATIVE — not authorized for this run
hypotheses.title: Along-strike basement-throw taper at concealed fault tips
layers: band 13: iso_grav_anom only; derived inverted basement depth
hypotheses.physical_signature: For each connected depth-HGM step segment at least 20 km long, sample signed 2 km normal throw every 400 m along strike. Require one polarity over the central 60% and a monotone or single-hump displacement envelope whose median absolute throw in each terminal 20% is <=0.20 of the segment maximum; do not use catalogue traces to define or orient segments.
hypotheses.why_missing_from_catalogue: A fault buried beneath basin fill can have a real basement displacement tapering to subsurface tips even when no surface rupture or scarp is mapped; the scale-space tip geometry is present in the inverted interface.
hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: A finite intrusive body or density sheet can produce edge responses that taper near its ends; this is an explicit ambiguity, not a claim that taper proves faulting.
hypotheses.differs_from_existing: Local H61 code thresholds pointwise throw and tests persistence across Gaussian scales 0/2/5; GEMSDOE52 R2 tests cross-layer normal orientation at 1/3/8 px, and H53/H54 test trace continuation. H61U-H2 instead tests the along-strike envelope of signed basement displacement at subsurface step tips, without band 15 or catalogue geometry.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: 2 of 3; low-to-medium potential, uncertain and unquantified
hypotheses.cost: medium (component graph plus fixed along-strike displacement-profile test)
hypotheses.data_obtainability: Only cached band 13 and the pinned competition grid are required locally; GP-1012 remains the separate, unavailable depth-scale calibration reference.

hypotheses.status: PROSPECTIVE, UNTESTED ALTERNATIVE — not authorized for this run
hypotheses.title: Local gravity source-class comparison: basement step versus buried density sheet
layers: band 13: iso_grav_anom only; derived inverted basement depth for candidate normals
hypotheses.physical_signature: At each candidate depth-HGM normal, fit the preregistered one-dimensional band-13 gravity profile with two label-free forward models: a Parker basement-interface step and a finite buried density-sheet/contact model. Retain a fault-step candidate only when the step model wins by a fixed information-criterion margin (BIC difference >=10), with all nuisance ranges frozen before any holdout evaluation.
hypotheses.why_missing_from_catalogue: A real basement offset under alluvial cover is not necessarily mapped at the surface; the gravity profile can still contain its source-shape signature.
hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: A finite-width mafic/granitic intrusive body or lithologic contact inside basement; the competing density-sheet forward model is intended to reject this non-fault cause.
hypotheses.differs_from_existing: Existing H61 methods detect, threshold, corridor, or corroborate depth-HGM edges; none compares raw gravity profiles against competing basement-interface-relief and intrabasement-density forward models. It uses no band 15 and no catalogue-derived feature.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: 3 of 3; uncertain/low potential because gravity source non-uniqueness may dominate
hypotheses.cost: high (two physical forward models, nuisance bounds, model-selection validation)
hypotheses.data_obtainability: Only cached band 13 and the pinned competition grid are required locally; GP-1012 is still needed for any depth-scale calibration and is not currently available in full.
